name: Museo Reina Sofía
notes: The Sabatini building (Francesco Sabatini's General Hospital, 18th century) as the museum since 1992: four storeys of granite base and plastered walls, rows of windows, pitched roofs, round a great garden court with trees and a fountain, set at its true angle (from the OpenStreetMap ground); Ian Ritchie's two glass-and-steel lift towers on the front toward Atocha; and Jean Nouvel's 2005 extension to the south-west, three buildings (library, exhibition halls, auditorium) round a court under one great cantilevered metal roof edged in red. From general knowledge of the buildings; no photographs were available. The roofs' material, which front carries the towers, and the Nouvel buildings' shapes and heights are approximations. Refined 30 Sep 2026 (no photographs reachable; the ground file's OpenStreetMap outlines and published descriptions): the Sabatini building moved 9 m west and 6 m south onto its outline, and the Nouvel extension 24 m west and 20 m north, onto the two blocks the ground shows beside it (a tall one of about seven storeys and a lower one) — which of Nouvel's three buildings is which is still guessed; the old building's cornices made pale limestone and its roofs blue-grey rather than black.
